verdict.rationale: IRS documents several sanctioned intermediary rails through which a provider can act for a company. A third-party designee can apply for an EIN with signed authorization from the responsible party. Authorized IRS e-file Providers have a published enrollment path (up to 45-day approval, fingerprinting for non-credentialed principals) to transmit via MeF, and IRIS A2A intake is gated by a Transmitter Control Code. Missing for 10: no independent or hands-on corroboration that the designee or provider rails work as described, and no evidence of a representative/power-of-attorney rail or of how far designee authority extends beyond EIN application.

support.subject: As a legal-ops lead, the service documents a sanctioned third-party rail — designees, authorized providers, registered agents, or representatives — through which a provider can act for my company

citations.quote: a third-party designee may apply, with signed authorization from the responsible party
Transmission requires becoming an Authorized IRS e-file Provider
it can take up to 45 days from the date of submission for the IRS to approve your e-file application
the A2A channel is gated by a Transmitter Control Code
